global_read: state/global.json (2026-09-03 12:59) shows a mixed but still net-cautious tape: Brent has pushed further up to $96.40 (+0.81% 1d, +15.08% 1mo) and WTI $92.16 (+1.26%/+14.71%), the oil shock still building rather than fading. S&P +0.46% and Dow +0.56% are green today and VIX at 15.14 (-0.39% 1d, -4.54% 1mo) is calm on the surface, which reads risk-on in isolation -- but Gold has jumped +3.67% in a single day (+12.22% 1mo) to $4,526.7, an unusually sharp safe-haven bid alongside green equities that signals hedging rather than conviction. BTC/ETH are both up modestly (+1.3-1.7% 1d), a soft risk-on cross-check. USD/PKR (277.31) and DXY (99.01) remain essentially flat -- the FX channel still has not cracked. Net: global equities are not confirming a clean risk-on signal (gold's spike undercuts it), oil keeps widening Pakistan's import-bill risk, and this sits on top of a confirmed 11.1% domestic CPI shock and a hawkish SBP into the Sept 14 MPC -- the desk reads today as risk-off, not risk-on, notwithstanding the green S&P print.
drivers: Pakistan's August 2026 headline CPI printed 11.1-11.15% YoY (PBS), up from July's 9.2% and more than triple August 2025's 3.56%, exceeding market forecasts and keeping the central bank wary per Bloomberg's 2026-09-01 coverage; forecasters (Growth Securities) see it easing to 9-10% in Sept/Oct but this print itself is a confirmed, well-above-target shock. Re-verified this run via https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-01/pakistan-inflation-exceeds-forecast-keeping-central-bank-wary and https://tribune.com.pk/story/2625171/august-inflation-seen-jumping-to-11

With CPI now confirmed at 11.1% against SBP's own 5-7% FY guidance, near-term cut odds for Sept 14 are effectively off the table and an extended hawkish hold is the base case. favored: refineries (ATRL/NRL/PRL) -- benefiting from higher crack-spread expectations at elevated crude (Brent $96.40), plus the pending refinery-upgrade policy tailwind; a narrower, more defensible expression of the oil move than E&P/OMC broadly

large, well-capitalized banks holding government paper -- the T-bill/PIB carry tailwind (6M now 11.90%, 10Y PIB 12.30%) was reinforced, not undercut, by today's auction, where the belly of the curve rose even as the short end eased, and by the hot CPI print removing near-term rate-cut risk ahead of the Sept 14 MPC
avoid: OMCs -- squeezed between a volatile, near-daily-reset pump price and rising import cost of the product itself as Brent keeps climbing
autos, cement and power/IPPs -- rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed; power/IPPs carry the added overhang of the unresolved circular-debt sticking point heading into the IMF's September review

small/thinly-capitalized banks and rate-sensitive high-leverage names -- the confirmed 11.1% CPI print removes any near-term rate-relief thesis and argues for an extended hawkish SBP stance at the Sept 14 MPC

broad cyclicals / index-chasing -- geo-risk radar rose to 63/100 'moderate' on higher energy-shock and safe-haven stress, reserves have not grown in over two weeks, and the domestic CPI shock stacks a second, confirmed negative on top of the oil shock; today's modest +0.09% PSX bounce is a stabilization, not a green light to add broad risk
